items.title: Ruth Brisbane interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 2, 2013
items.q: I remember falling asleep on the train one night and Diahann Carroll’s father woke me up.

ctx.x: And how would you get home after that?

Believe it or not I’m amazed when I worked in Manhattan, all the way up to 125th, I took the subway home. I can’t imagine doing that today, or twenty years ago I couldn’t imagine doing that. And I had six blocks to walk from the subway in Brooklyn. I remember falling asleep on the train one night and Diahann Carroll’s father woke me up. He was a conductor on the A train, and that’s the train I took home to Brooklyn. And he woke me up and he said, “I believe you get off soon.” I will thank that man forever.…
Yeah, so those are some pretty late nights and you can watch the sun come up almost.
